title: A Structural FHMM for Interpretable Disease Trajectories in T2DM
abstract: arXiv:2608.24328v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In this work, we propose a structural variant of the Factorial Hidden Markov Model (FHMM) for the analysis of disease trajectories in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The model represents a patient's latent health state as a combination of multiple independent, simultaneously evolving components, associated with comorbidities and lab results. This structured latent representation facilitates the identification of clinically meaningful patient states and clustering of common disease trajectories. We evaluate the proposed approach using The IQVIA Medical Research Data incorporating data from THIN, a Cegedim database of anonymized electronic health records (EHR), identifying patients with a first-ever prescription for a non-insulin antidiabetic drug (NIAD) between January 2006 and December 2019. The model identifies multiple clinically coherent latent components corresponding to known patterns of diabetes-related complications

translated_title: 一种用于2型糖尿病可解释疾病轨迹的结构化因子隐马尔可夫模型
translated_abstract: 本文提出了一种因子隐马尔可夫模型（FHMM）的结构化变体，用于分析2型糖尿病（T2DM）患者的疾病轨迹。该模型将患者的潜在健康状态表示为多个独立且同时演变的组件的组合，这些组件与合并症和实验室结果相关联。这种结构化的潜在表示有助于识别具有临床意义的患者状态，并聚类常见的疾病轨迹。我们使用IQVIA医学研究数据（包含THIN，一个Cegedim匿名的电子健康记录（EHR）数据库）评估了所提出的方法，识别出2006年1月至2019年12月期间首次处方非胰岛素抗糖尿病药物（NIAD）的患者。该模型识别出多个临床连贯的潜在组件，对应于已知的糖尿病相关并发症模式。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种结构化因子隐马尔可夫模型，通过将患者健康状态分解为多个独立组件，实现了对2型糖尿病疾病轨迹的可解释性分析，并识别出与临床并发症相关的模式。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a structural Factorial Hidden Markov Model that decomposes patient health states into independent components, enabling interpretable analysis of T2DM disease trajectories and identification of clinically relevant complication patterns.
